thread:
marc_support: Opening case C-4321 — customer reporting intermittent 502/504 to our hosted API only when calling over an AWS Interface VPC Endpoint (VPCE). Works from internet, fails from their VPC. Symptoms: TLS handshake errors or upstream timeouts.

alice_support: Got it. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl -v), dig output for the API hostname from their VPC (and from internet), traceroute/tracert if available, and VPCE id + whether Private DNS was enabled? Also SGs attached to the endpoint ENI?

marc_support: Pasting what customer provided (sanitized). They ran these from an EC2 in the same subnet as the VPCE: \n```
$ dig +short api.redwood.com @10.0.0.2
vpce-abcdefg-0123456-1a2b3c.vpce-svc-123456.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com.\n$ curl -v https://api.redwood.com/health
* Connected to 10.0.10.45 (10.0.10.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* Server certificate: CN=service.internal.redwood
* SSL: certificate subject name 'service.internal.redwood' does not match target host name 'api.redwood.com'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name 'service.internal.redwood' does not match target host name 'api.redwood.com'
```
They also saw intermittent `504` when certificate matched but backend timed out.\n\njason_infra: Two quick checks that often trip this: 1) Is the VPCE doing Private DNS rewrite so `api.redwood.com` resolves to the VPCE dns name? 2) Is there an NLB vs ALB in front of the service and where is TLS terminated? If NLB is terminating TLS (or not) SNI and cert SANs matter.

maria_networks: Also check the endpoint ENI route table entries and source/dest check. We've seen central TGW route precedence accidentally capturing traffic so health checks hit wrong subnet. Confirm the route table for the subnet doesn't have a more specific route to a TGW/NAT that overrides local ENI.

marc_support: Customer confirms Private DNS was ON for the VPCE and they left hostname usage unchanged. They have an NLB in front of the service doing TLS termination and certificates are internal CNs (service.internal.redwood). Their curl shows the CN mismatch above. Tcpdump they captured shows clienthello with SNI `api.redwood.com` followed by server cert for `service.internal.redwood` and connection close. Snippet: \n```
Client Hello: SNI: api.redwood.com
Server Certificate: CN=service.internal.redwood
TCP RST after cert
```
They also ran `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.10.45:443 -servername api.redwood.com` and received the same cert.\n\njason_infra: Root cause looks like TLS hostname mismatch due to Private DNS pointing `api.redwood.com` to the VPCE which routes to an NLB configured with a certificate that doesn't include `api.redwood.com`. Internet traffic likely routes to our public ALB/cert which has the right SANs. Two remediation paths: \n- Update the NLB/ALB cert to include `api.redwood.com` (preferable), or\n- Switch to TLS passthrough so SNI reaches the upstream ALB that has correct certs, or\n- Disable Private DNS and use the public hostname (less ideal).

alice_support: Also verify VPCE security group egress rules — if the NLB performs health checks from nodes in different AZs those source IPs must be allowed. If the SG or local firewall blocks healthcheck probes you'll get 502/504 flapping because target group appears unhealthy.

maria_networks: Side note: If customer uses a proxy or egress allowlist in their VPC, ensure proxy rewrites SNI or forwards original host header correctly. Some proxies terminate TLS and re-emit with different SNI which can break routing to the correct backend cert.

marc_support: Sent customer repro commands to run and asked for results: \n```
# dig from inside VPC
dig +short api.redwood.com @10.0.0.2\n# confirm cert served by VPCE IP
openssl s_client -connect 10.0.10.45:443 -servername api.redwood.com | openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer -text | sed -n '1,4p'\n# quick curl test forcing host header
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.com:443:10.0.10.45 https://api.redwood.com/health
```
I also asked them to capture `tcpdump -n -s0 -w /tmp/vpce.pcap port 443` for a few minutes.\n\nsre_bot: Suggested runbook items added to ticket: CHECK_VPCE_PRIVATE_DNS, CHECK_LOAD_BALANCER_CERT, CHECK_VPCE_SG_HEALTHCHECK_ALLOW, VERIFY_ROUTE_TABLE_PRECEDENCE.\n\njason_infra: If customer confirms Certificate CN mismatch and they cannot rotate certs quickly, immediate workaround: create a dedicated ALIAS/CNAME in their Private DNS that points `api.redwood.com` to the public ALB (bypass VPCE) or update the NLB to present a cert with `api.redwood.com` SAN. For customers behind strict egress allowlists: ensure outbound to our public ALB IPs/hosts or allow VPCE-to-backend paths.

alice_support: Can you ask them to also check their endpoint SG inbound/outbound — we need: inbound port 443 from their client subnets and inbound from load-balancer nodes for healthchecks, outbound to our backend IPs if NAT/proxy in place. Sample security-group rules we recommended: \n- Inbound: TCP 443 from 10.0.0.0/16 (client subnets) + load balancer nodes (AZ ranges)\n- Outbound: TCP 443 to 0.0.0.0/0 (or specific Redwood egress IPs if locked down)

marc_support: Customer ran tests, confirmed: dig resolves to vpce host, openssl shows internal cert without `api.redwood.com`. They will rotate certs on NLB to include SAN for `api.redwood.com`. They asked if we can accept connections without reconfiguring on our side — short answer: no, TLS hostname must match cert. I've asked for ETA on rotation and scheduled a follow-up.

maria_networks: If they hit more timeouts after cert rotation, check MTU (don't forget path MTU when VPCE + NAT + proxy). Also confirm `source/dest` check on ENI is enabled (should be enabled unless you're using a NAT/forwarding appliance).

marc_support: Closing loop: next steps — customer will rotate certs to include api.redwood.com or switch to ALB/terminate TLS with public cert. If problem persists after rotation, I will escalate to eng-infra and share tcpdump + pcap. :thumbsup:

alice_support: Thx — marking as monitoring. If they share pcap, tag #eng-infra and #netops.

marc_support: (after 2h) customer confirmed rotation fixed the CN mismatch and error rate dropped to 0. No further action. Closing ticket C-4321. :white_check_mark:
